newsitem.title: FRANCE: French police detain 11 suspected Islamists.
newsitem.headline: French police detain 11 suspected Islamists.

text.p: Police on Wednesday detained 11 people in the Paris region suspected of ties to militant Islamic groups which may have helped a French gangster flee to Bosnia.
Police said the 11, detained in the suburbs of Seine Saint-Denis and Nanterre, were held for questioning on the orders of anti-terrorism magistrate Jean-Louis Bruguiere.
But searches at their homes turned up little evidence and no weapons apart from a shotgun, police said.

The swoops were aimed at rooting out an Islamist network which allegedly helped Lionel Dumont, a gangster with fundamentalist extremist ties, to flee France for Bosnia after evading a police shootout in the northern city of Roubaix in March 1996.

Four other individuals, suspected of being part of a gang of guerrillas who organised robberies to finance fundamentalist activities, died in the Roubaix shootout when the house in which they were hiding caught fire and burned to the ground.
After evading police for a year, Dumont was detained in Bosnia last March after allegedly trying to hold up a petrol station and carrying out unspecified "terrorist" acts.

Police said Wednesday's raids were triggered by documents seized in December raids in Roubaix suggesting that Islamic networks were preparing false identity papers to help guerrillas conceal their identities from police or at border crossings.
France often detains suspects for questioning and releases them a few hours later, in a bid to destabilise Moslem groups.

France has been the target of a string of bombings blamed on Algerian extremists, most recently a bomb last December in the Port Royal underground station in Paris that killed four people and injured dozens.

While no evidence has turned up indicating a link between the December bombing and Roubaix, Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre told the French daily Le Figaro this week that the bombing might be linked to unspecified gangsters and terrorists who were working together.
He said there were still many unanswered questions over the station bombing, even though the probe had made progress.
French investigators suspect Algerian Islamic militants, who claimed responsibility for a previous wave of bombings in 1995 that killed eight people, were behind the station bombing.
Algerian Moslem militants accuse France, the former colonial power, of propping up the Algiers government.
About 60,000 people have died in fighting in the North African country since early 1992, when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
